detail.longDescription: 🚨 BREAKING: A NORTH KOREA-LINKED GITHUB WORM HAS INFECTED OVER 7,600 REPOSITORIES, AND IT CAN HIDE MALWARE WITHOUT LEAVING A SUSPICIOUS CODE DIFF. Dubbed PolinRider, the self-spreading malware has been identified in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories across 2,330 accounts. Attackers use stolen developer credentials to rewrite existing commits while preserving the original author, message and timestamps. The malicious code is hidden behind hundreds of invisible tabs, making it easy to miss during code review. And this isn't just theoretical. Researchers found that the worm infiltrated pull requests at AsyncAPI, CircuitVerse and Open Food Facts. At CircuitVerse, the malicious code actually executed inside GitHub Actions, and 40 desktop installers were published from compromised build runners. They remained downloadable for over a month before being removed. The malware can also execute through build scripts or automatically when a developer opens an infected project in VS Code with automatic tasks enabled. It steals credentials, spreads to other repositories and uses Ethereum blockchain transactions to locate its command-and-control servers. Here's the worrying part: attackers briefly inserted the malware into open pull requests, allowed CI workflows to execute it, then removed it. The final code looked clean. Full technical investigation, attack chain, affected projects and detection guidance ↓ https:// thecybersecguru.com/news/polin rider-worm-github-supply-chain-attack/ # GitHub # PolinRider # CyberSecurity # SupplyChainAttack
